baseline.reason: Reviewed baseline from main after the #694 refactors. Each oversized owner reviewed as cohesive gets its size at this commit plus 10% review headroom, so the check asks for a review when growth accumulates rather than on every small change. Growth since the refactors was reviewed for cohesion, not size: owners that grew within their own responsibility are recorded as reviewed, and the two that gained a second responsibility are deferred with follow-up issues and no headroom.

remediation: Maintainability is the goal; file size is a review signal, not the definition of good design. A file that outgrows its ceiling needs a review of its responsibilities: extract a genuinely separate responsibility, keep the change net-neutral by moving cohesive behavior, or raise the ceiling in a reviewed policy change with a reason, a follow-up when extraction is deferred, and a re-review condition. Raising the ceiling of a cohesive owner is better than splitting it into fragments. A Danger acknowledgement cannot bypass enforcement.
anti_gaming: Do not compress formatting or combine statements solely to lower physical LOC.
Do not delete validation, safeguards, tests, comments, or useful type precision to satisfy the check.
Do not move unrelated behavior into a generic helper.
Do not disguise handwritten code as generated output or add it to an exclusion.
Do not split a cohesive file into fragments that every task must still read together.
Review reduced responsibility and navigation burden, not line-count reduction alone.
